correctness.rationale: The white-complement skew-fort obstruction lemma is proved in both directions. Two separately implemented exhaustive algorithms cover all 65536 initial sets for each exactly specified 16-vertex graph; their full polynomials and 316 minimal forts per graph agree. The C++ implementation also checks obstruction equivalence for every white mask. The Python program validates all 666 certificate data rows; no sampling or infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The novel scientific claim is exact equality of full skew-forcing polynomials with differing smallest skew-fort geometry on a standard cospectral strongly regular pair. The original 2010 skew rule, earlier ordinary forcing census and same-pair positive-semidefinite forcing study do not imply the new skew statement. Relevant full text and indexed mathematical sources were compared with explicit quantifier and forcing-rule distinctions. Historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The canonical nonisomorphic cospectral (16,6,2,2) pair tests which graph invariants distinguish strongly regular twins. Full skew-forcing polynomial coincidence in the presence of divergent minimal four-fort geometries is structurally informative, with a complete natural finite invariant and complete minimal-fort size spectrum; these are not routine restatements of the ordinary or positive-semidefinite forcing results.
